children: Deal will be funded through cash and a new USD 338 million senior debt facility arranged by a bank group

Essar Energy Transition Retail (EET Retail), part of Cheshire-based Essar Energy Transition Fuels (EETF), has agreed to acquire 100 per cent of SGN Retail, a UK independent forecourt operator, in a Euro 250 million (USD338 million) deal.

The transaction will add 118 forecourt locations to EET Retail’s existing portfolio of 117 sites, taking its total network to 235 fuel forecourts, the company said in a statement. The combined network will have annual throughput of more than 650 million litres.

The transaction will be funded through a combination of cash and a new Euro 250 million senior debt facility arranged by a bank group comprising First Abu Dhabi Bank, Macquarie Bank, Mizrahi Tefahot Bank, Natixis, OakNorth Bank, Royal Bank of Canada, SMBC Bank International and Sound Point Capital Management.

Essar Energy Transition said it is pursuing a model in the UK that combines fuel manufacturing with the sale of fuels to consumers. It said the transaction will create the second-largest UK forecourt network that is backwardly integrated with fuel production.
The acquisition is expected to support EET Retail’s plan to supply domestic fuel directly to 800 forecourts by 2031, representing around 9 per cent of the UK market, according to the company.
EET Retail said demographic growth, an increase in multi-car households and a decline in the number of forecourts in the UK are factors behind its investment in the sector.

The company also said rerouting fuel refined at the Stanlow refinery directly into its forecourts would allow UK-refined fuel to be distributed more efficiently to domestic consumers and support domestic fuel supply security.
